natural_language_statement:
If $S$ is a Sidon subset of $X$ of maximum size, then $|X| \le 3|S|^3$.

Adding any $x$ outside $S$ must break the Sidon property, and since $S$ itself is Sidon the broken relation has to involve $x$. Either $x + b = c + d$ with $b, c, d \in S$, so $x = c + d - b$, at most $|S|^3$ values, or $x + x = c + d$, so $x = (c+d)/2$, at most $|S|^2$ values. With the $|S|$ elements of $S$ that gives $|X| \le |S| + |S|^2 + |S|^3 \le 3|S|^3$, the last step needing $|S| \ge 1$, which holds unless $X$ is empty.
source: The cube-root bound is folklore; this is its counting step
